title: Review: How fast? The rate of chemical change; How far? The extent of chemical change
source: Questions and terms copied unchanged from the site's bank, except where marked for IB Diploma Chemistry (status of the source: ai-reviewed-reverified-gate-verified-2026-09-30-awaiting-human-signoff). Terms and clues: R2.3#c02 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R2.2#c01 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R2.3#c10 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition; R2.2#c10 bank term, clue written for the game from the bank's definition. The matching task revisits terms from the worlds it reviews, in a new mix. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Closed system
items.clue: No matter can enter or leave, though energy can.

items.label: Rate of reaction
items.clue: The change in concentration of a species per unit time.

items.label: Position of equilibrium
items.clue: The relative amounts of reactants and products in the mixture.

items.label: Activation energy, Ea
items.clue: The minimum that colliding particles need for a successful change.

questions.stem: The concentration of a reactant, R, is followed at constant temperature. A graph of [R] (y-axis, mol dm⁻³) against time (x-axis, s) is a curve that starts at 0.0500 mol dm⁻³, becomes less steep and reaches zero at 1500 s. The curve passes through the point (300 s, 0.0220 mol dm⁻³). A tangent drawn to the curve at t = 300 s passes through the points (0 s, 0.0370 mol dm⁻³) and (600 s, 0.0070 mol dm⁻³). What is the rate of reaction at t = 300 s?

options.text: 7.33 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹
5.00 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹
3.33 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹
9.33 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹

questions.stem: Sample P is neon gas at 40 °C. Sample Q contains twice as many krypton atoms as P and is at 20 °C. Which statement comparing the kinetic energies of the atoms in the two samples is correct?

options.text: The mean kinetic energy of the atoms in P is greater than that in Q, but only by about 7%.
The mean kinetic energy of the atoms in P is twice the mean kinetic energy in Q.
The atoms in Q have the greater mean kinetic energy, as krypton atoms are heavier.
The atoms in Q have the greater mean kinetic energy, as Q contains more atoms.

questions.explanation: Mean kinetic energy is proportional to the absolute temperature: 40 °C = 313 K and 20 °C = 293 K, so the ratio is 313/293 = 1.07. The size of the sample does not affect the mean energy per atom. Neither the number of atoms nor their mass affects the mean kinetic energy per atom.

questions.stem: Hydrogen iodide decomposes: 2HI(g) → H₂(g) + I₂(g). A sample of hydrogen iodide is compressed to half its volume at constant temperature. What is the effect on the rate of reaction, and why?

options.text: It is unchanged: there are equal amounts of gas on both sides of the equation, so pressure has no effect.
It increases: the compressed molecules collide more energetically, so more collisions exceed Ea.
It increases: a larger amount of H₂ and I₂ can now form from the same amount of HI as before.
It increases: collisions become more frequent, and the fraction with E ≥ Ea is unchanged.

questions.stem: For a reaction with Ea = 50 kJ mol⁻¹, raising the temperature from 300 K to 310 K almost doubles the rate. Which statement gives the main reason for this large increase?

options.text: A much larger fraction of all the collisions now have energy equal to or greater than Ea.
The particles move faster, so they collide more often, and more collisions give more reactions.
The activation energy decreases as the temperature rises, so more of the collisions succeed.
Every particle gains the same amount of energy, which carries many more of them past Ea.

questions.stem: For a hypothetical endothermic reaction, the uncatalysed forward activation energy is 280 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔH = +110 kJ mol⁻¹. A catalyst lowers the forward activation energy to 230 kJ mol⁻¹. What is the activation energy of the catalysed reverse reaction?

options.text: +170 kJ mol⁻¹
−110 kJ mol⁻¹
+120 kJ mol⁻¹
+340 kJ mol⁻¹

questions.explanation: The products lie 110 kJ mol⁻¹ above the reactants and the catalysed maximum lies 230 kJ mol⁻¹ above the reactants, so the reverse barrier is 230 − 110 = 120 kJ mol⁻¹. The catalyst lowers the forward and reverse activation energies by the same 50 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.stem: Some liquid bromine is placed in a flask, which is then stoppered and kept at constant temperature. The brown colour of the vapour above the liquid deepens at first and then stays constant. Which statement about the flask once the colour is constant is correct?

options.text: Bromine still evaporates and condenses, and the two processes occur at equal rates.
Bromine has stopped evaporating, because the vapour above the liquid is saturated.
The system cannot be at equilibrium, because no chemical reaction takes place.
The concentration of Br₂ is now the same in the liquid and in the vapour.

questions.stem:
Methanol can be made from carbon dioxide and hydrogen in a homogeneous gas-phase equilibrium:
CO₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ CH₃OH(g) + H₂O(g)
Which is the equilibrium constant expression for this reaction?

options.text: K = [CH₃OH]/([CO₂][H₂]³)
K = [CH₃OH][H₂O]/([CO₂][H₂])
K = [CH₃OH][H₂O]/([CO₂]·3[H₂])
K = [CH₃OH][H₂O]/([CO₂][H₂]³)

questions.explanation: Correct. All four species are gases in a single phase, so every concentration appears: products over reactants, each raised to the power of its coefficient. 3H₂ gives [H₂]³, and H₂O(g) is a gaseous product whose concentration changes, so [H₂O] stays in the numerator.

questions.stem: For the reaction X(g) ⇌ Y(g), K = 1.0 × 10¹⁵ at 298 K. Which statement about this reaction at 298 K is correct?

options.text: At equilibrium, the mixture is made up almost entirely of X.
At equilibrium, almost all of X has been converted into Y.
At equilibrium, X and Y are present in similar amounts.
The large value of K shows that equilibrium is reached quickly.

questions.explanation: K ≫ 1, so [Y]/[X] = 1.0 × 10¹⁵ at equilibrium: the position of equilibrium lies far to the right and the reaction goes almost to completion.

questions.stem:
In a sealed bottle of carbonated water at constant temperature, carbon dioxide gas above the liquid is in equilibrium with dissolved carbon dioxide:
CO₂(g) ⇌ CO₂(aq)
When the cap is removed, gas escapes from the space above the liquid and bubbles of CO₂ form in the liquid. Which statement explains the formation of the bubbles?

options.text: The pressure of CO₂(g) falls, so the equilibrium shifts to the left.
Opening the bottle lowers K, so less CO₂ can stay dissolved.
The equilibrium was static while sealed, and restarts on opening.
CO₂ leaves the liquid until its former gas pressure is restored.

questions.stem: Magnesium ribbon reacts with excess hydrochloric acid, and the hydrogen is collected in a gas syringe. A graph of the volume of hydrogen (y-axis, cm³) against time (x-axis, s) is a curve that is steep at first, becomes less steep and levels off at 60 cm³ at 100 s. The curve passes through the point (20 s, 34 cm³). A tangent drawn to the curve at t = 20 s passes through the points (0 s, 10 cm³) and (40 s, 58 cm³). What is the rate of reaction at t = 20 s?

options.text: 1.70 cm³ s⁻¹
0.60 cm³ s⁻¹
0.83 cm³ s⁻¹
1.20 cm³ s⁻¹

questions.stem: Two reactant molecules in a gas collide with a combined kinetic energy greater than the activation energy, Ea, of the reaction, but they do not react. Which statement explains this?

options.text: No catalyst was present, and a reaction cannot take place at all without one.
They collided with an orientation that did not bring the reacting atoms together.
Their combined energy was less than the size of the enthalpy change of reaction, ΔH.
No spark or heating had first supplied the activation energy to start the reaction.

questions.explanation: A successful collision needs both energy equal to or greater than Ea and a proper orientation. With enough energy but the wrong collision geometry, the atoms that must bond do not meet, so no reaction occurs.

questions.stem:
Hydrogen and iodine are heated in a sealed flask at constant temperature until the amount of hydrogen iodide no longer changes:
H₂(g) + I₂(g) ⇌ 2HI(g)
Which statement must be true of the mixture at this point?

options.text: No HI forms or decomposes now, as both reactions have stopped.
HI forms and decomposes at equal rates, so its amount stays the same.
The concentrations of H₂, I₂ and HI have become equal to each other.
Half of the hydrogen and iodine has been converted into hydrogen iodide.

questions.explanation: The system is in dynamic equilibrium: in the closed flask the forward and backward reactions continue at equal rates, so the concentrations of H₂, I₂ and HI are constant although the reactions have not stopped.

questions.stem: Which statement correctly distinguishes a reaction intermediate from a transition state in a multistep reaction?

options.text: A transition state can be isolated if the reaction is stopped quickly enough, just as an intermediate can.
An intermediate is present at the start and is re-formed at the end; a transition state is used up.
An intermediate lies at an energy minimum between steps; a transition state is at a maximum and cannot be isolated.
An intermediate appears in the overall equation for the reaction; a transition state does not.

questions.explanation: An intermediate is formed in one step and used in a later one, and sits in a dip on the energy profile, so it has a finite lifetime and can in principle be detected. A transition state sits at a peak, with bonds partly broken and partly formed, and cannot be isolated.

questions.stem: A proposed mechanism for the reaction H₂(g) + I₂(g) → 2HI(g) is: step 1: I₂(g) ⇌ 2I(g) (fast); step 2: H₂(g) + 2I(g) → 2HI(g) (slow). Which statement about molecularity in this mechanism is correct?

options.text: Step 2 is bimolecular, as it involves two different reacting species, H₂ and I.
The slow step is termolecular, as one H₂ molecule and two I atoms must all collide together in it.
Step 1 is termolecular, as three particles, one I₂ molecule and two I atoms, appear in it.
The overall reaction is bimolecular, as one H₂ molecule collides with one I₂ molecule.

questions.stem: The initial rate of the reaction A + 2B → C was measured at constant temperature. Experiment 1: [A] = 0.010 mol dm⁻³, [B] = 0.020 mol dm⁻³, initial rate = 1.5 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. Experiment 2: [A] = 0.020 mol dm⁻³, [B] = 0.020 mol dm⁻³, initial rate = 6.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. Experiment 3: [A] = 0.020 mol dm⁻³, [B] = 0.060 mol dm⁻³, initial rate = 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. What is the rate equation?

options.text: rate = k[A]¹[B]²
rate = k[A]⁴[B]³
rate = k[A]¹[B]¹
rate = k[A]²[B]¹

questions.stem: The rate equation for a reaction is rate = k[A][B]². At constant temperature, the concentrations of A and B are both doubled. By what factor does the rate increase?
questions.explanation: The factors multiply: doubling [A] (first order) multiplies the rate by 2¹ = 2, and doubling [B] (second order) multiplies it by 2² = 4, so the rate increases by 2 × 4 = 8, which is 2 raised to the overall order, 3.

questions.stem: The rate equation for a reaction is rate = k[A]²[B]. When [A] = 0.020 mol dm⁻³ and [B] = 0.050 mol dm⁻³, the rate is 3.0 × 10⁻⁵ mol dm⁻³ s⁻¹. What is the value of k?

options.text: 0.030 mol⁻² dm⁶ s⁻¹
1.5 × 10⁻² mol⁻² dm⁶ s⁻¹
6.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ mol⁻² dm⁶ s⁻¹
1.5 mol⁻² dm⁶ s⁻¹

questions.stem: The rate constant of a reaction varies with absolute temperature according to the Arrhenius equation, k = Ae^(−Ea/RT). A student plots ln k (y-axis) against 1/T (x-axis) for one reaction over a range of temperatures. Which describes the graph?

options.text: A horizontal line, as k is a constant for a given reaction
A straight line with a negative gradient, equal to −Ea/R
A straight line with a negative gradient, equal to −Ea
A straight line with a positive gradient, as k rises with T

questions.explanation: Taking natural logarithms gives ln k = −(Ea/R)(1/T) + ln A, which has the form y = mx + c. The graph is a straight line with gradient −Ea/R and y-intercept ln A. Because the gradient is negative, ln k increases as 1/T decreases: k increases with temperature.
